purpose: Separate measured scheduling effects from residual disagreement between full-fight simulation and ordinary Java.
prospective: Use the next completed perfect-aim native scouting and first promotion panels after season 23. No openings from those panels have been inspected. Show scouting and promotion errors separately.
shape: Same positions, both seats, actual native policy weights, perfect aim, and recorded added RTT. W-tap on the same openings is a separate control.
comparisons: ClockPrediction fixed schedule sampled across 32 entity orders and phases
First 20 intervals on each of the three recorded clocks repeated, 128 trials
Post-game replay using complete native tick timestamps and repeating the final 20 intervals if a simulated fight lasts longer, 128 trials
outcome: Mean squared error against the Java match point (win 1, time-limit draw 0.5, loss 0), by fighter and RTT, plus overall.
interpretation: Complete timestamps became available during the recorded fight. Their use is an offline timing diagnostic. There is no claim that it is a prediction available before a fight.
training: These recorded calendars and native action traces are excluded from learner inputs, training opponents' observations, and rewards.
